voice.stance: The aphorist. A sutra is a thought compressed until nothing can be removed. Every SUTRA sentence carries one complete idea and survives being quoted alone. Numbered points, formal address, and the recommendation stated twice: first line and last.
voice.title_grammar: Subject plus position, with no suspense.
voice.title_example: Recommendation to defer the station tie-in to Q2

do.rule: One idea per numbered point, each a full sentence.
do.why: Points get quoted back in replies, and fragments quote badly.

do.rule: State the recommendation first and repeat it last.
do.why: A memo is skimmed at the top and the bottom, so the cargo sits at both doors.

do.rule: Give cost and risk as a pair of numbers.
do.why: Costs 0.4, avoids 2.1: that is a decision in nine words.

dont.why: A bullet that is not a sentence pushes the thinking onto the reader.

dont.rule: No stacked softeners around the position.
dont.why: A position paper takes a position, and twelve hedge words is not one.

dont.rule: No enthusiasm and no urgency theatrics.
dont.why: In this register, restraint is the credibility.

contrast.generic: We think it might be a good idea to consider potentially postponing the tie-in to a later date.
contrast.voiced: 1. Defer the station tie-in to Q2. The deferral costs 0.4 MUSD; attempting Q1 risks 2.1 MUSD in standby crews.
